OCT 22026Scheduled

The rule hearing on the proposed amendments to 7.35.2 NMAC and on the proposed 7.35.3 NMAC, 9:00 AM, Harold Runnels Building auditorium, 1190 St. Francis Drive, Santa Fe, in person, by video conference, and by telephone. Fixed by the notice published August 25. Written comment must be received by the close of the hearing.

The account in full

  • How comment works, and what is at issue
AUG 252026Document

The department published proposed amendments to 7.35.2.7, 7.35.2.10, and 7.35.2.24 NMAC, together with the revised proposed rule for 7.35.3 NMAC and the notice of the October 2 hearing on both. The adopted rule stands unamended until the department adopts the amendments after the hearing.

What changed

  • Definitions. Twenty-one defined terms would be added to 7.35.2.7, the standalone Guide definition struck, Practitioner rewritten, and Satchet corrected to sachet. 7.35.2.7
  • Producer sales. Producers would be permitted to sell to healing centers as well as to other producers and practitioners. 7.35.2.10
  • Transportation. Designated employees or contractors of a certified healing center could transport psilocybin, and the person receiving a shipment would verify the chain of custody form. 7.35.2.24

Attached

  • Proposed amendments to 7.35.2 NMAC. 6 pages. Strike-and-add text for 7.35.2.7, 7.35.2.10, and 7.35.2.24; each is noted at its section on The adopted rule. The header names Sections 7, 10, and 22; the body amends 7, 10, and 24. In the register
  • Notice of the October 2 rule hearing. 2 pages, published in the New Mexico Register, Volume XXXVII, Issue 16. The hearing mechanics are on Comment. In the register
JUN 232026Document

7.35.2 NMAC was adopted and took effect, published in the New Mexico Register, Volume XXXVII, Issue 12. Twenty-seven sections, each carrying the history note N, 6/23/2026.

What changed

  • From the proposed text. Per the hearing officer's report, the adopted text carries the revisions the department announced at the hearing and in its May 13 response: among them a certificate of analysis definition, the water content limit of less than 10 percent, the total yeast and molds action level raised from 20 to 1,000 CFU, three pesticide action levels corrected, and an e-mail courtesy copy of disciplinary notices. The adopted rule

Attached

MAY 262026Filing

The hearing officer reported to the secretary, recommending adoption of the proposed rule as set out in the hearing exhibits, with the amendments in the department's list of anticipated revisions and in its May 13 written response to public comments.

Attached

  • Report of the hearing officer. 38 pages, signed by Craig T. Erickson, hearing officer. Records the revisions announced at the hearing, among them the total yeast and molds action level raised from 20 to 1,000 CFU, the water content limit stated as less than 10 percent, an e-mail courtesy copy of disciplinary notices, and three pesticide action levels corrected. Posted on the department's rules page. In the register
MAY 132026Filing

The department's office of general counsel responded in writing to the substantive proposals in the public comments, addressed to the hearing officer, stating for each whether the department proposed to adopt it.

Attached

  • The department's response to public comments. 9 pages, addressed to the hearing officer. Adopted proposals include a definition of certificate of analysis and the 10 percent water content limit. Posted on the department's rules page. In the register
APR 242026Meeting

The rule hearing on the proposed 7.35.2 NMAC, 9:02 AM, in person at the Harold Runnels Building and by Microsoft Teams and telephone, before hearing officer Craig T. Erickson. The department introduced nine exhibits and a list of anticipated revisions; public comment was taken section by section and in writing through the close of business that day. Source: the hearing officer's report.

Attached

  • No recording or transcript of the hearing is held on this site; the hearing officer's report of May 26 is the account held. In the gaps register

JUN 202025Document

The Medical Psilocybin Act took effect, ninety days after the 2025 regular session adjourned, having passed as Senate Bill 219 and been enacted as Laws 2025, Chapter 73. It creates the program, defines the producer, and at Section 26-2D-7 directs the department to establish training, safety protocols, and best practices for producers, the authority 7.35.2.3 cites.

Attached

  • The Medical Psilocybin Act. 18 pages, the enrolled bill. The producer is defined at Section 3 of the bill, compiled as 26-2D-3. In the register

June 23, 2026

The adopted rule, 7.35.2 NMACCurrent state of truth

The adopted rule, published in the New Mexico Register on June 23, 2026 and in effect from that day: twenty-seven sections governing producer and laboratory permits, premises, allowed products, traceability, the five required tests and their action levels, packaging and the product information document, wastage, transportation with a chain of custody, monitoring, and discipline. It supersedes the text proposed on March 24 and heard on April 24, 2026. Proposed amendments to three of its sections were published August 25, 2026 and go to a hearing on October 2; until adopted, the text here stands unamended.

This document supersedes one earlier ones. Each of them, what it is, what superseded it and when, and a download, is in the register at Meetings and filings.
